public_rationale: The initial data recorded 130 ADS-involved crashes, with repeated reports involving Waymo, Transdev and Cruise. That supports the contextual claim that these developers were experiencing repeated incidents. It does not establish that their systems caused the crashes, that they were unusually unsafe, or that Level 5 systems were being deployed.
limitations: Support is for repeated crash involvement, not technical fault or comparative danger.
The original report was inaccessible to read_page; the assessment uses its TRB summary and contemporary AP reporting.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Companies working on full (Level 5) self-driving are having plenty of problems, per NHTSA ADS data.

statement.excerpt: Because it shows that the people who really claim to be working on full self-driving (which Tesla waffles on1) are having plenty of problems of their own.
statement.document_title: Will Tesla ever “Solve” Full Self Driving?

from_speaker: the people who really claim to be working on full self-driving
are having plenty of problems of their own
our_interpretation: The referenced graph makes this a claim about repeated reported crash involvement among ADS developers in NHTSA's initial June 2022 release.
'Problems' is read as repeated crash involvement requiring attention, without assuming that the ADS caused each crash or was less safe than human driving.
The target period is July 2021 through May 15, 2022, the reporting window underlying the graph discussed in the post.
ADS reporting covers Levels 3–5; it does not establish that the reported vehicles were operating at Level 5.
criteria.support_condition: The initial release documents repeated crash involvement across ADS developers, including developers such as Waymo and Cruise.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The initial release shows no repeated crash involvement among those developers, or the apparent pattern results from a misreading of the data.

evidence.explanation: The record confirms repeated ADS crash involvement in the initial reporting period. Its abstract defines reportability by ADS use within 30 seconds of a crash, not by a finding of ADS fault.

evidence.locator: Section 'Fully autonomous vehicles: 130 crashes, none serious', first paragraph
evidence.publisher: Associated Press, republished by New Hampshire Public Radio
evidence.explanation: The developer counts establish repeated involvement rather than an isolated incident. The article also reports that most ADS crashes involved rear impacts and that 108 had no reported injuries, limiting any inference about severity or ADS fault.
